analysis: This PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the date (line 3) and adds a sentence at lines 627-629 of the head. The sentence says the conversation live-test report also records delta files and greedy output tokens. It also documents DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 as a way to get a complete-file baseline. No source, configuration, workflow or runtime behavior changes. I checked the change against the encrypted SSD prefix-cache threat T-041, covering assets A-001 and A-004. The documented test setup still uses env -i, an isolated ephemeral cache and an exclusive GPU, and the nearby text says never to use production cache roots or keys. The new flag appears only in test guidance. It is not documented as a production default and does not alter the production gate, TTL, HMAC lookup naming, DBK3 metadata, or the KEK purge. Test output now includes delta file counts and greedy output tokens, which may expose content-adjacent data. The runner uses public fixed-date prompts and isolated reports, so no leak of consumer data is shown. Open question for later passes: the incremental-checkpoint/delta file feature is implemented elsewhere. Whether it keeps nothing prompt-derived on disk beyond the keyed lookup tag, and whether its TTL, LRU and write-budget behavior are unchanged, is outside the supplied evidence. If a production code change introduced it, review it against the T-041 detection_hint.
